HDR='    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    lo = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    def rate(m):
        return float(r[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0'
mk(){ # name desc body
cat > $D/$1.py <<EOF
# name: $1
# description: $2
def test_statistic(df):
$HDR
$3
EOF
}
mk single_example_same_last_digit_far "Yes-rate for single-example sets on targets >=20 away sharing the example's last digit; observed above null means the model under-produces digit generalisation from one example." '    x = ex[:, 0]
    m = (n == 1) & (np.abs(t - x) >= 20) & (np.mod(t, 10) == np.mod(x, 10))
    return rate(m)'
mk single_example_near_far_gradient "Single-example sets: yes-rate for targets within 10 of the example minus yes-rate for targets >30 away; observed above null means people's similarity gradient is steeper than the model's." '    d = np.abs(t - ex[:, 0])
    return rate((n == 1) & (d <= 10) & (d > 0)) - rate((n == 1) & (d > 30))'
mk wide_vs_narrow_span_fill "Multi-example sets: yes-rate for targets inside [min,max] when span>=40 minus when span<=15; observed below null means people fill wide spans less than the model predicts." '    inside = (t >= lo) & (t <= hi) & (n >= 2)
    span = hi - lo
    return rate(inside & (span >= 40)) - rate(inside & (span <= 15))'
mk upward_vs_downward_extension "Multi-example sets: yes-rate for targets 1-10 above the max minus targets 1-10 below the min; nonzero observed vs null means an asymmetric extension the model misses." '    up = (n >= 2) & (t > hi) & (t <= hi + 10)
    dn = (n >= 2) & (t < lo) & (t >= lo - 10)
    return rate(up) - rate(dn)'
mk round_target_bias "Among sets with no multiple-of-10 example, yes-rate for multiple-of-10 targets minus other targets outside the example range; observed above null means people over-accept round numbers relative to the model." '    has10 = np.any(np.mod(np.nan_to_num(ex, nan=1.0), 10) == 0, axis=1)
    out = (~has10) & ((t < lo) | (t > hi))
    return rate(out & (np.mod(t, 10) == 0)) - rate(out & (np.mod(t, 10) != 0))'
mk arithmetic_rule_outside_boost "Sets of >=2 all-even examples: yes-rate for even minus odd targets outside the example range; observed above null means people use parity rules more than the model." '    alleven = np.all(np.mod(np.nan_to_num(ex, nan=2.0), 2) == 0, axis=1) & (n >= 2)
    out = alleven & ((t < lo) | (t > hi))
    return rate(out & (np.mod(t, 2) == 0)) - rate(out & (np.mod(t, 2) == 1))'
mk shared_last_digit_multi_boost "Sets where all (>=2) examples share a last digit: yes-rate for outside-range targets with that digit minus other outside-range targets; observed vs null tells whether the model over- or under-produces noticed-digit rules." '    d = np.mod(np.nan_to_num(ex, nan=-1.0), 10)
    d0 = d[:, 0]
    same = (n >= 2) & np.all((d == d0[:, None]) | np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    out = same & ((t < lo) | (t > hi))
    return rate(out & (np.mod(t, 10) == d0)) - rate(out & (np.mod(t, 10) != d0))'
mk trial_position_yes_drift "Overall yes-rate in trials above the median trial_index minus below; observed different from null means response bias drifts over the session in a way the model does not capture." '    ti = df["trial_index"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    med = np.median(ti)
    return rate(ti > med) - rate(ti <= med)'

content.text:
All 8 test statistics are now in `iter_2/critique/test_stats/`. None of them has an import statement; they only use the `np` and `pd` already in scope, which is what knocked out every statistic in the first attempt. I ran each one once on the observed data, outside the harness. Each returned a finite number in about 0.01–0.03 s. I did not run the posterior-predictive check itself, so there are no p-values yet.

| Statistic | What it tests | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| `single_example_same_last_digit_far` | After one example, how often people say yes to targets at least 20 away with the same last digit. The model holds back digit rules after a single example; this checks whether people do too. | 0.333 |
| `single_example_near_far_gradient` | After one example, yes-rate for targets within 10 minus yes-rate for targets more than 30 away. This compares how steeply yes-answers fall off with distance in people versus the model. | 0.400 |
| `wide_vs_narrow_span_fill` | Yes-rate for targets inside the examples' range when the range is wide (40 or more) minus when it is narrow (15 or less). | −0.130 |
| `upward_vs_downward_extension` | Yes-rate for targets up to 10 above the highest example minus targets up to 10 below the lowest. | −0.061 |
| `round_target_bias` | For sets with no multiple of 10, yes-rate for multiples of 10 minus other targets outside the range. | −0.028 |
| `arithmetic_rule_outside_boost` | For sets of all-even examples, yes-rate for even minus odd targets outside the range. | 0.218 |
| `shared_last_digit_multi_boost` | When all the examples share a last digit, yes-rate for targets with that digit minus other targets outside the range. This tests the model's one new mechanism directly. | 0.446 |
| `trial_position_yes_drift` | Yes-rate in the second half of the session minus the first half. | −0.052 |

Each file's `# description:` line says which way a gap between the observed value and the model's predictions should be read.
